newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat drops on selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat drops on selling pressure.

text.p: Milling wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) eased on selling pressure after trading in a very wide range of some 800 forints on Thursday, traders said.

"At the start of trade everybody expected prices to rise due to overnight Chicago rises, but the trend turned round and prices, especially for longer maturities, dropped significantly," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap brokerage.
He added the weather was improving after cold and rain over the last few days, allaying fears of difficult harvesting, and this weighed on prices.
Milling wheat prices finished 70 to 330 forints per tonne lower with August ending at 20,550, down 150, December at 21,900, down 270 and May at 23,970, down 330 forints, respectively.
Maize futures edged down by 70 to 100 forints for most positions except May which dropped 300 forints to 20,900 and July 1998 which rose 80 forints to 22,000.
Total grains turnover jumped to 1,709 lots or 736.4 million forints from Wednesday's 955 lots or 415.9 million forints.
Milling wheat futures accounted for the bulk of the turnover in volume terms with 932 lots, followed by maize with 491 lots.
